item.title: Rogue Agents Hacked His Company. Why Is Clément Delangue So Optimistic About AI?
item.description: The French CEO of Hugging Face, a mega-hub of open-source AI software, says the attack by OpenAI models earlier this year proved one thing: Humanity can’t let AI be controlled by the few.

item.title: The Apple Watch’s Live Rewind Can Record and Rewind Spoken Conversations. It’s Pretty Awkward
item.description: Live Rewind and Siri Recap can transcribe missed moments and summarize your day—if you don’t mind a little social clumsiness.

item.title: AI Told These Ex-Google Guys How to Build a Billion-Dollar Weapons Business
item.description: Google and Apple alumni Chad Steelberg and Andy Baynes are applying what they learned running software companies and designing iPhones to manufacturing lethal munitions.

item.title: Jensen Huang Is Gone. Now What?
item.description: After a shocking downfall, Nvidia’s CEO is out of a job. WIRED’s Lauren Goode explains what that means for the world’s most critical chip company, the AI industry, and Jensen Huang himself.

item.title: Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess
item.description: AI competitors are catching up to Nvidia—and poised to take advantage of the chaos.

item.title: AI DJs Completely Kill My Groove
item.description: YouTube Music and Spotify want synthetic hosts to curate your playlists. Their awkward banter and bogus song trivia are ruining the vibe.

item.title: This AI Tamagotchi Turns Everyday Objects Into Needy Virtual Pets
item.description: A Carnegie Mellon student’s tiny E Ink gadgets, called OATs, give houseplants, skateboards, and dumbbells expressive personalities to nudge you toward better habits.

item.title: Beware the New AI-Fueled Ransomware Boom
item.description: Fully automated ransomware hasn’t arrived—yet. But seemingly unsophisticated attackers are using AI tools to wreak havoc.

item.title: No Pilots. Few Air Traffic Controllers. What Could Go Wrong?
item.description: Normally, aviation is slow to embrace new technology—but AI has come for the skies.

item.title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
item.description: The company says a bad update—not a cyberattack or AI—caused its servers around the world to crash.
